Current milestone state — updated 2026-11-26 (end of day). main is 73c4bd9; the v1.4.0 milestone has 0 open bugs.

VERSION: v1.3.0 stable (2026-07-23) still current — the installed rvr is 1.3.0, so bootstraps stay pre-#191 until v1.4.0 ships. Everything since is unreleased on main (list in CHANGELOG [Unreleased]). UNTIL 1.4.0 IS INSTALLED: `rvr set k <<EOF` and `rvr set k < file` fail on 1.3.0 (fixed by #221) — pipe the value or pass "$(cat file)"; plain `rvr get` fails on an entry whose text holds an unresolved dollar-brace reference (fixed by #230) — read it with `get -s`.

THEME: v1.4.0 = FORUM (#186, picked 2026-09-04). Milestone 'v1.4.0 — Forum' is the release gate: every issue in it closes before the tag. SCOPE (owner decisions 2026-11-24): #189 and #186 ARE v1.4.0 release items — a cut proposed that day (front page only, #189 and steps 3–4 to the next minor) was REVERSED, do not re-propose it. OPEN FEATURE WORK: #189, #215 steps 2–3 (its unreadable-file gaps were split to #270 and deferred), #226 (open questions, builds on #140), #227 (compaction, builds on #84); #186 closes last. Design: docs/design-189-forum-threads.md — seven owner decisions O1–O7, still unanswered; slices 1–2 can start once O1 is answered.

BUG STOP RULE (owner, 2026-11-26): a finding blocks 1.4.0 only if it lets a flagged command run unasked or loses or corrupts data; everything else is filed for after 1.4.0. Each bug PR gets one independent review plus one confirmation pass, no open-ended rounds. Done check: `gh issue list --milestone "v1.4.0 — Forum" --label bug`. PLAN (owner, 2026-11-26: no rush for 1.4.0 — make it bulletproof by method, not by more review rounds): (1) bring the end-to-end gate fuzzer into the repo and run it on gate changes (#290); (2) one name resolver for alias+scope used by every command (#284 class, #260); (3) gate and run from one snapshot of both stores (#289 class, the mid-run store rewrite); (4) wrapper handshake — the wrapper evals only when the binary proves source mode (#281 class, #287); (5) clear the formerly deferred bugs: #260, #268 (set --confirm and remove are still two writes), #270, #271, #277, #285, #286, #287, #291. Then the Forum features, then the release-checklist audit. Each step is its own PR with one review + one confirmation pass. FINISH LINE for 1.4.0: milestone 0 bugs, fuzzer green, a fresh security audit finds no gate weakening or data loss, every remaining issue fixed or explicitly accepted by the owner.

MERGED 2026-11-26 (detail in CHANGELOG): #250–#253 and #263–#266 closed the review findings listed here before (exec output re-scan #242, MCP token replay #243, Unicode-fold write #246, project list false over a global flag #241, remove dropping a flag #244, stack traces #249, concurrent writers #254, lock-timeout excerpt #261). #269: a rename is one transaction under both store locks (#259 #245 #247). #276: `confirm set` lists a flag under the stored spelling; a global-only entry's flag goes in the global list, falling back to the project list with a warning when the global list can't be read or written (#255 #256 #248 #257). OWNER-ACCEPTED DIFFERENCES from main in #276: an explicit `confirm remove` fully ungates where main kept a duplicate spelling, and `confirm remove -G` clears a flag that #256 put in the global list. #275 closed #213: config.json stores only settings that differ from the default ([[arch.config]]). #278: every store write ends on an even epoch, an entry and a namespace under one key both survive a whole-store write, and the suite can't write the checkout's own store ([[arch.storeTransactions]], [[context.testDataLeaks]]). Gate rules: [[context.confirmGate]].

SECURITY AUDIT 2026-11-26 (security-audit workflow on 26bc13e): 6 findings confirmed, 1 rejected (MCP chain:true). Owner: all 6 block 1.4.0. Checking fix A found a seventh, #284 (with -G a project alias picked which global entry set/rm/rename/confirm remove acted on; also in 1.3.0), and its review an eighth, #289 (the collect pass that feeds the gate returned a partial trace when its reference walk threw, while exec ran on through its cache; also in 1.3.0). OWNER-ACCEPTED DIFFERENCE from main in the #280 fix: a global entry's dollar-brace reference with a :- default, whose key exists only in the project, now takes the default, where main resolved the project's entry and asked for confirmation; nothing flagged runs. Also accepted: a reference split across `a:b` run segments no longer resolves (#291). MERGED: #288 (73ba22a) closed #281 #282 #283 — `run --source` prints only the command, the wrapper (v2) passes --json/--dry through and puts --source right after `run`, install replaces only a byte-exact shipped wrapper, backups dirs must be real directories, the undo never reads through a link, an irregular sidecar is STORE_UNREADABLE (an irregular _confirm.json gates every run). #292 (73c4bd9) closed #279 #280 #284 #289 — see [[arch.scope]], [[arch.interpolation]], [[context.confirmGate]], [[context.aliasCollision]]. Both had one review + one confirmation pass; the reviewers' end-to-end fuzzer (CLI+MCP, scored on what ran) found #289 where the repo harness could not (#290).

GHSAs: PUBLISHED GHSA-cchh-h245-wgr7 and GHSA-62qw-v74v-wxc6 (#158, #159; patched 1.3.0). NINE DRAFTS HELD until 1.4.0 is tagged: GHSA-9653-mh42-mfjj (#234), GHSA-vj74-g5wx-8hvv (#242), GHSA-qrch-7p2g-xv8q (#241), GHSA-3g67-gwmx-3xp5 (#279), GHSA-cpx3-5chf-vwcw (#280), GHSA-g233-7583-cf8g (#281), GHSA-j27x-crw5-35fq (#282, high), GHSA-ww8w-4986-74pj (#284, low), GHSA-pmp8-xv6h-2mr9 (#289, low). The release checklist's Post-release step publishes them; source records in docs/security/advisory-*.md, scoping in [[context.ghsaExecOnRead]]. PR bodies and commits name the issue, never a draft GHSA id. The 1.3.0 CHANGELOG never mentioned the #158/#159 fixes (owner's call whether to add them).

SMALL UNDECIDED ITEMS, no issue yet: `get --json` returns the raw value for a `:?` guard or a cycle where plain `get` fails; a value that completes a cycle is stored without a word, and both entries then fail every read; default `lint` in a project does not see a global entry in a namespace the project also has. CHANGED IN #230 WITHOUT AN OWNER DECISION (say so if asked): `get --source --json` returns the stored text.

RELEASE v1.4.0: docs/release-checklist.md carries the steps, the security-audit gate and the smoke lines. Beyond it: exercise the MCP surface deliberately (#191, #218, #275 changed it; MCP gets no ambient use); compiled-binary validation per [[context.bunCompileGotchas]]; stale-tag comm check per [[context.releaseTagNamespace]]; watch the release workflow (first run of the action bumps). The owner's Mac holds a hand-set bootstrap_max_response_bytes of 140000 — after installing 1.4.0, `rvr config unset` it, then read a week of context rows (pinned/indexed/demotedNamespaces) to calibrate the pinned default.

UNEXERCISED UNTIL THE NEXT TAG: the release.yml bumps (#200 upload-artifact 7.0.2, #201 download-artifact 8.0.2, #214 action-gh-release 3.0.4) — SHAs checked against upstream tags, never run. #191 went in on 1549 tests + CodeQL, no code review. Dependency handling: [[context.dependabotOverrides]]; [[context.dependencyScanBlind]].

EXTERNAL DATASET 2026-10-30 → issues #202–#213, see [[context.channelFit]]. Overlaps with prior filings: D2=#192, D4⊂#137 (#207 is the cheap partial), D7=#190.

SOAK: the v1.3.0 soak hit the 14d cap without an eval; the Sept theme pick superseded it. Next soak pegs to v1.4.0.

CARRIED CANDIDATES (unmilestoned): #137 session derivation, #136 retrospective, #139 audit value controls, #140 miss-paths, #84 entry health, #42 git-freshness, #45 attribution; ex-Find #13 fuzzy finder, #43 boolean search, #47 rvr diff; from the 2026-10-30 dataset #208 --append, #209 find-and-replace, #210 SessionStart hook recipe.

RELEASE MAP: v1.4.0 Forum (#186) / v1.5.0 Reach (#6 #49) / v1.6.0 Share (#115) / v1.7.0 Scale (#44 #48 #143) / v1.8.0 Surfaces (#51) / v2.0.0 (#128, Sept 2027).

TIER-3 REFACTOR BACKLOG: import-pipeline unification, rename/copy core, paths.ts walk dedup, registerTool migration, load() snapshot memo. NON-ENGINEERING: [[project.commercialContext]], launch comms, visual identity.
